name: crypto_hash
description: Compute a cryptographic hash of a value with the given algorithm (case-insensitive). Supported algorithms: blake2b-512, blake2s-256, blake3, keccak{224,256,384,512} (original Keccak, as used by Ethereum), md5, ripemd160, sha1, sha2-{224,256,384,512}, sha2-512/224, sha2-512/256, sha3-{224,256,384,512}, shake128, shake256 and sm3 — `crypto_algorithms()` lists them with their digest lengths. Accepts strings, BLOB and string-backed types (JSON, BIT), every integer and floating-point type, DECIMAL, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIME, TIME_TZ, TIMESTAMP variants, INTERVAL, UUID, ENUM, and lists or fixed-size arrays of those. Different DuckDB types of the same numeric value produce different hashes; UUIDs hash as their 16 RFC 9562 bytes, DECIMALs by unscaled value regardless of width, and ENUMs by label.

examples.description: SHA-256 of a string, displayed as hex
BLAKE3 of arbitrary integer
Hash a list — each VARCHAR/BLOB element's length is hashed before its content
Keccak-256 as used by Ethereum (differs from sha3-256)
A UUID hashes as its 16 bytes, the same as hashing unhex() of its digits
DECIMAL hashes by unscaled value, so the declared width doesn't matter
A fixed-size ARRAY hashes the same as the equivalent LIST

name: crypto_hash_agg
description: Order-deterministic aggregate hash. Hashes column values sequentially in the ORDER BY order — yielding the same digest as `crypto_hash` over an equivalent ordered list. Accepts the same scalar types as `crypto_hash` (UUID, DECIMAL, ENUM, BOOLEAN, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL, …) and works as a window function. ORDER BY is required and checked when the query is planned (`Hash aggregation requires a distinct total ordering`); NULL values are an error, so skip them with `FILTER (WHERE x IS NOT NULL)`. Returns NULL for an empty group. Useful for dataset checksums, change detection, and Merkle-style hierarchical hashing.

examples.description: Per-department checksum of employee IDs
examples.code:
SELECT department,
       lower(to_hex(crypto_hash_agg('sha2-256', employee_id ORDER BY employee_id))) AS dept_hash
FROM employees
GROUP BY department;

examples.description: Aggregate hash matches list hash exactly when input is the same ordered set

columns.name: (crypto_hash_agg('sha2-256', "value" ORDER BY "value") = crypto_hash('sha2-256', CAST(list_value(1, 2, 3, 4, 5) AS INTEGER[])))

examples.description: Skip NULLs explicitly with FILTER

name: crypto_hmac
description: Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC). Combines a secret key with a message under a specified hash algorithm — used for message integrity and API request signing. The key and message may each be VARCHAR or BLOB, so keys from `crypto_random_bytes` or `unhex()` work directly. blake3 uses its keyed mode and needs a 32-byte key; shake128 and shake256 are not supported. Verify a MAC with `crypto_equals`.

examples.description: HMAC-SHA256 over a message with a secret key
RFC 4231 test case 1, with a BLOB key

name: crypto_random_bytes
description: Cryptographically secure random bytes from OpenSSL's RAND_bytes. Suitable for keys, salts, nonces, and other cryptographic material. Length must be between 1 and 4 GB − 1; large outputs count against DuckDB's `memory_limit`.

examples.description: 32 random bytes — an AES-256 key
16-byte salt displayed as hex

name: crypto_hash_xof
description: Extendable-output hash: returns `length` bytes (1 to 4,294,967,295) of a blake3, shake128 or shake256 digest. A shorter output is a prefix of a longer one, and the default length (32 bytes for blake3 and shake128, 64 for shake256) matches `crypto_hash`. Accepts the same input types as `crypto_hash`. Large outputs count against `memory_limit`.

examples.description: 100 bytes of SHAKE256
The default length matches crypto_hash

name: crypto_equals
description: Constant-time comparison of two VARCHAR or BLOB values, using OpenSSL's `CRYPTO_memcmp`. Returns true when they hold the same bytes. Use it instead of `=` when verifying an HMAC or other secret, so timing doesn't reveal how many leading bytes matched. NULL in either argument returns NULL.

examples.description: Verify an HMAC
examples.code:
SELECT crypto_equals(crypto_hmac('sha2-256', 'k', 'm'), crypto_hmac('sha2-256', 'k', 'm')) AS valid,
       crypto_equals(crypto_hmac('sha2-256', 'k', 'm'), crypto_hmac('sha2-256', 'k', 'n')) AS tampered;

examples.description: Compares bytes, so VARCHAR and BLOB can be mixed

name: crypto_pbkdf2
description: PBKDF2-HMAC key derivation ([RFC 8018](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8018)). Derives `length` bytes (1 to 1,048,576) from a password and salt with the given HMAC algorithm and iteration count (at least 1). Password and salt accept VARCHAR or BLOB. blake3 is not supported. Prefer `crypto_argon2` for new password storage; use PBKDF2 where FIPS compliance or interoperability requires it.

examples.description: RFC 6070 test vector (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, 4096 iterations)
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 40-byte output

name: crypto_hkdf
description: HKDF extract-and-expand ([RFC 5869](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5869)). Derives `length` bytes from high-entropy input key material, an optional salt, and a context `info` string; `length` is at most 255 × the digest length (8,160 bytes for sha2-256). Key, salt and info accept VARCHAR or BLOB. HKDF is fast, so it is for deriving keys from a secret, not for hashing passwords.

examples.description: RFC 5869 test case 1
examples.code:
SELECT lower(to_hex(crypto_hkdf('sha2-256',
         unhex('0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b'),
         unhex('000102030405060708090a0b0c'),
         unhex('f0f1f2f3f4f5f6f7f8f9'),
         42))) AS okm;

examples.description: RFC 5869 test case 3: empty salt and info

name: crypto_scrypt
description: scrypt password-based key derivation ([RFC 7914](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7914)). `n` is the CPU/memory cost and must be a power of 2, `r` the block size and `p` the parallelism; output is `length` bytes (up to 1 MiB). Password and salt accept VARCHAR or BLOB. Working memory (128 × n × r bytes) is reserved against DuckDB's `memory_limit` before it is allocated.

examples.description: RFC 7914 test vector (n = 1024, r = 8, p = 16)

name: crypto_argon2
description: Argon2 password hashing ([RFC 9106](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9106)). `variant` is 'argon2id' (recommended), 'argon2i' or 'argon2d' (case-insensitive); `memory_kib` is the memory cost in KiB (at least 32) and `parallelism` the number of lanes. The salt must be at least 8 bytes; output is `length` bytes (up to 1 MiB). Password and salt accept VARCHAR or BLOB. Working memory is reserved against DuckDB's `memory_limit` before it is allocated.

examples.description: Argon2id with 2 iterations, 64 MiB and 4 lanes
A small, fast configuration for tests

name: crypto_algorithms
description: Lists every hash algorithm the extension knows, with its family, implementation (openssl or blake3), digest length in bytes, whether it is an extendable-output function, whether it can be used with `crypto_hmac`, and whether the linked OpenSSL library provides it. md4 is listed as unavailable because it lives only in OpenSSL's legacy provider.

examples.description: The SHA-3 family and its extendable-output relatives
examples.code:
SELECT name, digest_length, is_xof, supports_hmac
FROM crypto_algorithms()
WHERE family IN ('sha3', 'shake')
ORDER BY name;

examples.description: Algorithms the linked OpenSSL doesn't provide
examples.code: SELECT name, available FROM crypto_algorithms() WHERE NOT available;

returnsTable.name: name
returnsTable.description: Algorithm name, as passed to crypto_hash and the other functions (case-insensitive).

returnsTable.name: family
returnsTable.description: Algorithm family, e.g. sha2, sha3, shake, keccak, blake2.

returnsTable.name: implementation
returnsTable.description: openssl, or blake3 for the vendored BLAKE3 library.

returnsTable.name: digest_length
returnsTable.description: Output length in bytes (the default length for XOFs); NULL when the algorithm is unavailable.

returnsTable.name: is_xof
returnsTable.description: Whether crypto_hash_xof can produce output of any length.

returnsTable.name: supports_hmac
returnsTable.description: Whether the algorithm can be used with crypto_hmac.

returnsTable.name: available
returnsTable.description: Whether the linked OpenSSL library provides the algorithm.
